title: Sweetcorn Fritters
subtitle: Golden corn fritters with spring onion and chilli
excerpt: Sweetcorn kernels in a light, crisp batter with spring onion, smoked paprika, and a little chilli. Fried until golden. Serve stacked with soured cream, avocado, and lime as a brunch or light lunch.

recipe.sourceNotes: Corn fritters are popular across the Americas and Pacific Rim, and were absorbed into British brunch culture through the Australian cafe tradition of the 1990s and 2000s. They are made by folding sweetcorn kernels, either fresh, tinned, or frozen, into a light flour, egg, and milk batter with seasoning. The result is crispier and lighter than a courgette fritter because the corn does not contain as much water. Fresh corn on the cob gives the best flavour when in season; tinned corn is a reliable alternative year-round.

content.text: The batter should be thick enough to hold the corn in clumps but not so heavy that the fritters feel stodgy. Do not over-fill the pan: cook in batches so the fritters have room to brown rather than steam. They are done when the edges are set and the underside is deep golden.
Whisk the flour, eggs, and milk together into a thick batter. Stir in the sweetcorn, spring onion, smoked paprika, chilli flakes, salt, and pepper.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Drop heaped tablespoons of batter into the pan, pressing gently to flatten. Cook for 3 minutes until the underside is deep golden. Flip and cook for a further 2 to 3 minutes. Cook in batches.
Drain briefly on kitchen paper. Serve with soured cream and lime wedges.
